findings.problem: The first card is visible when the reader taps 'salesman' at [7:104], before he is even named at [7:106]. It already says he is 'keen on betting and short-tempered'. The betting trait is the point of Holmes's trick, which is only explained at [7:150], and his temper first shows at [7:121]. There is no later snapshot to carry these details.
findings.evidence: [7:150] "When you see a man with whiskers of that cut and the ‘Pink ’un’ protruding out of his pocket, you can always draw him by a bet"
findings.fix: First card body (from [7:104]): "A poultry salesman at Covent Garden Market who supplied the Alpha Inn with its two dozen geese." Add snapshot from [7:150]: "A sharp-faced, short-tempered poultry salesman with one of the largest stalls in Covent Garden Market. He refuses to say where the Alpha's geese came from, but Holmes provokes him into a bet and he shows his ledger: they came from Mrs. Oakshott of Brixton Road."

findings.problem: 'Holmes traces him through a card...' suggests Holmes has already found him. At [7:61] Holmes has only the card and the initials and is about to advertise. Baker turns up only at [7:80].
findings.evidence: [7:61] "So now we must set ourselves very seriously to finding this gentleman"
findings.fix: "The man whose battered hat and Christmas goose Peterson picked up in Tottenham Court Road. All Holmes has to identify him are a card on the goose reading ‘For Mrs. Henry Baker’ and the initials ‘H. B.’ in the hat."

findings.problem: Tapping 'John Horner' at [7:59] shows his age (26), his previous conviction and his protests of innocence. All three first appear in the newspaper report at [7:60]. The gap is only one paragraph and none of it is concealed, but the previous conviction is a case fact, not an ordinary identity fact.
findings.evidence: [7:59] "John Horner, a plumber, was accused of having abstracted it from the lady’s jewel-case. The evidence against him was so strong that the case has been referred to the Assizes."
findings.fix: First card body (from [7:59]): "A plumber accused of stealing the Countess of Morcar’s blue carbuncle at the Hotel Cosmopolitan. The evidence against him is strong enough that the case has been sent to the Assizes." Add snapshot from [7:60] with the current first-card text.

findings.problem: 'Holmes lets him go, expecting him to flee' attributes a motive Holmes never states. Ryder offers to leave the country at [7:186], but Holmes's reason at [7:213] is that Ryder will not appear against Horner and is too frightened to go wrong again.
findings.evidence: [7:213] "this fellow will not appear against him, and the case must collapse ... This fellow will not go wrong again; he is too terribly frightened."
findings.fix: "The hotel attendant who stole the blue carbuncle and let Horner be blamed. He hid the stone in a goose at his sister’s, took the wrong bird, and lost track of it. Holmes lets him go: without Ryder’s evidence the case against Horner must collapse, and Holmes judges him too frightened to go wrong again."

findings.where: bound 'my sister' at [7:188] (shows [7:141] card); snapshot gated [7:190]
findings.problem: At [7:188] the reader learns that Mrs. Oakshott is Ryder's sister, and the 'my sister' mentions there are bound to her. Tapping them still shows the ledger-only card, which does not explain the link, because the relationship snapshot is gated two paragraphs later at [7:190]. The name 'Maggie' ([7:194], [7:201]) is never explained on any card.
findings.evidence: [7:188] "I made for my sister’s house. She had married a man named Oakshott, and lived in Brixton Road, where she fattened fowls for the market."
findings.fix: Add snapshot from [7:188]: "James Ryder’s sister, married to a man named Oakshott. She fattens fowls for the market at 117 Brixton Road and sold Breckinridge twenty-four geese on 22 December." Keep the [7:190] snapshot, and append to it: " Ryder calls her Maggie." (or move that sentence to a new snapshot from [7:194]).

findings.problem: At [7:60] the newspaper names 'Inspector Bradstreet, B division', who gave evidence about Horner's arrest. The card shown is the story-6 snapshot ('on duty at the Bow Street police station ... Hugh Boone'), which says nothing about his part in this story and names a different station from the text.
findings.evidence: [7:60] "Inspector Bradstreet, B division, gave evidence as to the arrest of Horner"
findings.fix: Add snapshot from [7:60]: "A police inspector who knows Holmes from the Hugh Boone affair. In the Hotel Cosmopolitan robbery he gave evidence at the police court about the arrest of John Horner."

findings.problem: 'A member of the household at Holmes’s Baker Street rooms' identifies her only vaguely. The passage implies she prepares Holmes's dinner (he will ask her to check the woodcock's crop). The same card carries into story 8, where she answers the door and lights the fire.
findings.evidence: [7:78] "I dine at seven. There is a woodcock, I believe. By the way, in view of recent occurrences, perhaps I ought to ask Mrs. Hudson to examine its crop."
findings.fix: Subtitle: "Of the Baker Street household" (unchanged). Body: "The woman who keeps house at Holmes’s Baker Street rooms and sees to his meals. Holmes jokes that he should have her check his dinner’s woodcock for jewels."

findings.problem: Tapping at [7:54] shows the hotel and the jewel-case theft ([7:58]–[7:59]) and the £1,000 reward ([7:55]). These are one to five paragraphs ahead and are backstory, not concealed. Noted only for consistency of gating.
findings.evidence: [7:54] "Not the Countess of Morcar’s blue carbuncle!"
findings.fix: Acceptable as is. For strictness: first card "A titled lady, owner of a famous blue carbuncle that has recently gone missing." plus snapshot from [7:60] with the current text.

findings.problem: The thread says 'something found in the goose turns the puzzle into a serious case'. With the Countess thread (blue carbuncle stolen) beside it, this gives away the [7:50] twist, the stone in the goose's crop, before the reader reaches it. The story title softens this, but the thread does not need to say it.
findings.evidence: [7:50] "See what my wife found in its crop!"
findings.fix: "Holmes treats a stray hat and Christmas goose as an intellectual exercise, reading a whole character from a battered hat, until an unexpected discovery turns the puzzle into a serious case."
